finding: The helixui.module file calls attach_library('helixui/hx-core') but helixui.libraries.yml defines the library key as 'helixui/core'. This name mismatch produces a Drupal fatal error on every page load and is a hard blocker for any Drupal integration.
recommendation: Change line 27 of helixui.module from 'helixui/hx-core' to 'helixui/core' to match the key defined in helixui.libraries.yml.

finding: CDN build artifacts (dist/cdn/) do not exist in the repository. The build:cdn script exists but has never been run, meaning the CDN integration path documented in INTEGRATION.md is entirely non-functional and unshippable for 3.0.0.
recommendation: Run 'pnpm --filter @helixui/library run build:cdn' and add CDN artifact production to the CI release pipeline so artifacts are published with every release.

finding: The hx-button SDC component.yml lists 'success' and 'link' as valid variant enum values, but the component TypeScript source defines variants as primary|secondary|tertiary|danger|ghost|outline only. Invalid enum values will silently fail or trigger devWarn in production Drupal sites. A separate documentation example also uses 'destructive' instead of the valid 'danger' value — enum drift is systemic.
recommendation: Audit all SDC component.yml files and documentation examples against the CEM. For hx-button, update variant enum to match source exactly: ['primary','secondary','tertiary','danger','ghost','outline']. Fix CDN INTEGRATION.md to use variant="danger".

finding: The drupal-starter package peerDependency for '@helixui/library' uses the 'workspace:^' protocol, which is only valid inside the monorepo. Any Drupal team installing @helixui/drupal-starter from npm will receive a broken package.json that fails resolution.
recommendation: Change the peerDependency to a semver range ('^3.0.0' for the 3.0 release) and verify package.json is correct before the npm publish.

finding: The root package.json 'customElements' field points to a worktree-specific path '.worktrees/feature-healthba-hx-carousel-document-25/packages/hx-library/custom-elements.json' that does not exist on CI or any collaborator machine. This is a stale artifact of a development session that was committed to source, and the field is semantically invalid at the root workspace level.
recommendation: Remove the 'customElements' field from the root package.json entirely. It belongs only in packages/hx-library/package.json where it already correctly exists.

finding: packages/drupal-behaviors/package.json uses 'main': 'src/index.js' with no exports map, no types field, and no build script. The package references source files as its published entry point and has no TypeScript declarations. A TypeScript consumer importing @helixui/drupal-behaviors receives no types and resolves to unbuildable source.
recommendation: Add a build script, exports map with types and import conditions, compile to dist/, and update main and files fields to match the established patterns in hx-library.

finding: The hx-change event is registered in HTMLElementEventMap with a union type 'CustomEvent<{ value: string } | { checked: boolean; value: string }>'. hx-text-input never dispatches a checked field — that shape belongs to hx-checkbox and hx-switch. This copy-paste error in the global event type registry produces incorrect type information for all consumers.
recommendation: Change the HTMLElementEventMap registration for hx-text-input's hx-change to CustomEvent<{ value: string }> only. Audit hx-select and hx-checkbox registrations for the same pattern (confirmed identical error in hx-select at line 760).

finding: hx-select registers its hx-change event in HTMLElementEventMap with the same incorrect union type as hx-text-input — including a 'checked' field it never dispatches. Additionally, the hidden native <select> element carries aria-label, aria-invalid, aria-describedby, and aria-required attributes while also having aria-hidden='true', making all those ARIA attributes dead markup that assistive technology ignores.
recommendation: Fix HTMLElementEventMap registration to CustomEvent<{ value: string }>. Remove all ARIA attributes from the aria-hidden native select element — ARIA semantics belong exclusively on the custom combobox element.

finding: hx-tooltip appends its _lightDomDescription element as a child of 'this' (the host element) via this.appendChild(). This directly mutates the consumer's light DOM, corrupting DOM structure, breaking CSS child selectors, and causing unexpected querySelector results on the parent. Web components must not modify their own light DOM children.
recommendation: Append the description element to document.body instead with visually-hidden positioning, and remove it in disconnectedCallback. This preserves host light DOM integrity while maintaining the aria-describedby cross-shadow reference.

finding: hx-dialog manages open/close state through both a component 'open' property and native dialog.showModal() calls, creating a dual state management layer. During rapid open/close cycles guarded by _isTransitioning, the native dialog element can fall out of sync with the component property. This is a structural race condition in the most critical interactive component in the library.
recommendation: Conduct a full architectural review of the open/close state management. At minimum, add an integration test that cycles open/close rapidly 10 times and asserts consistency between this.open, this._dialogEl.open, and aria-modal.

finding: hx-date-picker.styles.ts is a single minified CSS string with no line breaks, checked in as source code. This makes the file impossible to review, diff, or maintain. The same file contains hardcoded rgba() color values in box-shadow fallbacks not behind any design token, breaking theme compatibility.
recommendation: Expand the stylesheet to properly formatted CSS. Replace all raw rgba() shadow values with semantic token references (e.g., var(--hx-shadow-sm)). Minification belongs in the build pipeline only.

finding: No Subresource Integrity (SRI) hash support is documented or provided for the CDN loading strategy. Enterprise healthcare clients under HIPAA and security audit requirements will require SRI hashes on all third-party script assets.
recommendation: Add SRI hash generation to the build-cdn.mjs script, output hashes to manifest.json, and document how to add integrity and crossorigin attributes to Drupal library entries.

finding: No Declarative Shadow DOM (DSD) or Lit SSR support is implemented or documented. Content rendered inside Shadow DOM is invisible to Drupal's render cache keying and search engines until JavaScript loads, creating SEO and render-cache correctness gaps that healthcare content teams will hit immediately.
recommendation: Evaluate @lit-labs/ssr and DSD for high-SEO content components (hx-card, hx-text, hx-breadcrumb). At minimum, document the SSR gap explicitly in the Drupal integration guide with clear SEO implications.

finding: Standalone Twig templates cover only 4 components (hx-button, hx-card, hx-text-input, hx-form) while 59 SDC wrappers exist. High-demand form components including hx-select, hx-checkbox, hx-textarea, hx-radio-group, and hx-dialog have no standalone templates for Drupal Form API override use.
recommendation: Generate standalone templates for the remaining form components — at minimum hx-select, hx-checkbox, hx-radio-group, hx-textarea, hx-dialog, and hx-alert.

finding: There is no Drupal behavior provided for hx-dialog AJAX compatibility. Drupal's AJAX system triggers dialog opens via ajax_command_open_dialog, but there is no documented or implemented bridge to hx-dialog's open property.
recommendation: Add a helixuiDialogAjax behavior that listens for Drupal's ajaxDialogBeforeCreate event and routes it to the corresponding hx-dialog open property, with documentation on replacing core dialog.ajax with hx-dialog.

finding: hx-phi-field renders PHI data masked by default, but the masked state is controlled entirely via Shadow DOM internals. Without JavaScript, the raw PHI value passed via the 'data' attribute is present in the DOM as a plain attribute value, readable by automated crawlers and accessibility tools. This is a HIPAA compliance concern in a healthcare library.
recommendation: Evaluate whether the PHI data attribute should be omitted from server-rendered HTML and injected only after JS verification, or document server-side masking as a required prerequisite for HIPAA compliance in Drupal's render pipeline.

finding: The turbo.json 'generate' task declares outputs as 'packages/hx-react/src/components/**' — an absolute path from the repo root rather than relative to the package. Turborepo resolves outputs relative to the package root, making this output declaration a no-op that defeats caching for the React wrapper generator entirely.
recommendation: Scope the generate task to the hx-react package-level turbo.json and set outputs to 'src/components/**' so caching is correctly scoped.

finding: The turbo.json 'test' task lists '.cache/test-results.json' as its only output but Vitest writes coverage data to '.cache/coverage/'. Turborepo caches the task without capturing coverage artifacts, causing stale coverage reads on cache hits and silently invalidating the coverage quality gate.
recommendation: Add '.cache/coverage/**' to the test task outputs array so Turborepo invalidates the cache when coverage data changes.

finding: pre-push-check.sh Gate 2 runs 'pnpm run format' and if formatting changes are detected, it commits them automatically using 'git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit' — bypassing Husky and commitlint, silently creating auto-format commits with a generic message, and violating the project's zero --no-verify policy.
recommendation: Remove the auto-commit behavior from the pre-push hook. Fail the hook with a message instructing the developer to run 'pnpm run format' and commit the result manually.

finding: packages/drupal-starter/package.json has no 'main', 'types', or 'exports' field and no 'build' or 'type-check' script. The package is effectively untyped and invisible to the Turborepo pipeline, relying entirely on a raw files array. This is inconsistent with the rest of the workspace and will break npm consumers.
recommendation: Either explicitly mark this package as a non-JS asset bundle and remove it from TypeScript tooling, or add proper exports, build, and type-check scripts consistent with the rest of the workspace.

finding: The hx-react package has 'prebuild': 'pnpm run generate' which runs the React wrapper generator before every build. The generator reads the library CEM, but on a cold clone the CEM doesn't exist yet, causing the prebuild to fail silently or generate an empty wrapper set. This cold-start dependency is not captured in the Turborepo pipeline.
recommendation: Remove the prebuild hook and instead enforce generate through Turborepo by making hx-react#build depend on @helixui/library#cem via a proper dependsOn in turbo.json, so Turborepo guarantees CEM existence before generation.

finding: The root package.json defines 25 'hooks:*' scripts (lighthouse-performance, vrt-critical-paths, animation-budget-check, etc.) that invoke tsx scripts but none are wired into Husky hooks, called from preflight, or referenced in CI. Their execution context and trigger conditions are entirely undocumented, making this potentially dead tooling.
recommendation: Either integrate each hook script into the appropriate quality gate with documentation, or delete them. Undocumented tooling creates false confidence and maintenance burden.

finding: The updated() lifecycle hook in hx-tabs casts changedProperties to Map<PropertyKey, unknown> and calls .has('_activePanel') on a @state() field. Lit's PropertyValues<this> does not surface @state() properties in changedProperties — only @property() declarations appear there. The .has('_activePanel') check will never be true, making _updateTabsAndPanels() unreachable from this lifecycle path.
recommendation: Remove the updated() override for _activePanel detection. Call this._updateTabsAndPanels() directly inside the _activePanel assignment in _activateTab(), which is the correct reactive pattern.

finding: hx-breadcrumb's _applyCollapse() method uses document.createElement('hx-breadcrumb-item') and injects the result into the consumer's light DOM via firstItem.after(). This directly mutates consumer-authored markup, will cause double-rendering, break SSR, and violate the encapsulation contract of custom elements.
recommendation: Move the ellipsis element entirely into the shadow DOM using Lit reactive state. Track _isCollapsed and _collapsedItemCount as @state() fields and render the ellipsis button in the shadow template alongside the slotted <ol>.

finding: hx-alert stores slot change handlers as nullable function references on instance fields and manages them manually in firstUpdated/disconnectedCallback. This pattern circumvents Lit's declarative template system and creates lifecycle management complexity that is error-prone during reconnection cycles.
recommendation: Replace manual addEventListener/removeEventListener with @slotchange=${this._handleActionsSlotChange} bindings directly in the render template. Delete the handler reference fields.

finding: hx-toast has two distinct code quality defects: (1) _toastEl uses non-null assertion with '!' while simultaneously typing the field as 'HTMLElement | null' — logically incoherent; (2) _emitHide() hardcodes a 300ms fallback setTimeout that must match the CSS transition duration but has no connection to it, creating a silent divergence risk.
recommendation: Remove the '!' assertion from _toastEl. Extract the 300ms constant to a named static field with a comment tying it to the CSS transition duration, or derive it from getComputedStyle.

finding: The public index.ts exports resetIdCounter (a function that breaks ARIA associations in live components if called at runtime) and HelixAuditController (an internal observability tool) as first-class public API. Exposing these risks consumer misuse and couples internal telemetry infrastructure to the public API surface.
recommendation: Remove resetIdCounter from the public index. Move HelixAuditController to a separate unstable entry point (@helixui/library/controllers) or remove it from the public bundle. Both should be addressed before 3.0.0 establishes the public API surface.

finding: hx-dialog defaults the 'modal' property to true. A boolean HTML attribute with a default of true violates HTML boolean attribute semantics — attribute presence means true, absence means false. '<hx-dialog>' without attributes is already modal, making the attribute non-meaningful as a toggle. Consumers cannot opt out of modal behavior via HTML alone.
recommendation: Default modal to false and require explicit opt-in via the modal attribute, matching HTML boolean attribute semantics. Alternatively, rename to non-modal with default false.

finding: Root package.json uses 'name': 'wc-2026', a stale placeholder predating the HELiX rebrand. The name creates confusion in Turborepo task filtering, error messages, and monorepo tooling output.
recommendation: Update 'name' to 'helix-monorepo' or '@helixui/monorepo' to match the published package scope.

finding: The lint task declares dependsOn: ['^build'] which requires a full transitive build of all dependencies before linting any package — adding 30+ seconds to what should be a fast feedback loop. The type-check task has the same pattern with no inputs declaration, invalidating the type-check cache on any file change across the entire workspace.
recommendation: Remove dependsOn: ['^build'] from the lint task — ESLint operates on source files directly. Add inputs scoped to ['src/**/*.ts','tsconfig*.json'] to the type-check task to narrow cache invalidation.

finding: hx-react package.json declares react in both 'dependencies' and 'peerDependencies'. The dependencies entry causes React to be bundled into the output for consumers who already have React, which will trigger duplicate React instance errors in production applications.
recommendation: Remove react from hx-react dependencies entirely. It belongs only in peerDependencies. @lit/react must remain in dependencies as it is a runtime requirement.

finding: The changeset baseBranch is set to 'main' but all feature work targets the 'dev' branch. Changeset CLI computes diffs against 'main', causing it to undercount changed packages on feature branches that have not yet promoted to main.
recommendation: Change 'baseBranch' to 'dev' in .changeset/config.json to match the actual branch that all feature work targets.

finding: The CDN template covers only 12 of 75+ components. CDN adopters of components outside those 12 have no documented integration path. The CDN template also lacks a helix-core library entry for the shared Lit runtime chunk that must load before per-component files.
recommendation: Extend the CDN template to cover all components via a generator script, and add a helix-core base library entry with documented loading order requirements.

finding: Drupal's native #states API does not detect changes on web component custom events (hx-change) — only native change/input events on standard form elements. Conditional field patterns fail silently unless teams discover and implement the helixuiConditionalFields behavior workaround.
recommendation: Add a prominent 'drupal-states-compatibility' note to the forms documentation, and ensure helixuiConditionalFields behavior is featured as the required replacement for #states when using HELiX form components.

finding: The document-token-adoption utility adopts tokens into the top-level document only. Components rendered inside Drupal iframes (CKEditor 5 editor iframe, Layout Builder preview iframes) will not receive design tokens and will render with no styling.
recommendation: Document this limitation and provide an ensureDocumentTokens() call pattern for CKEditor 5 and iframe-embedded contexts, with a code example for the editor.js configuration.

finding: Multiple Wc* deprecated type aliases are re-exported from the index (WcBadge, WcContainer, WcDivider, WcNav, WcSwitch, WcTag, WcTheme, WcTreeView, WcTreeItem) without a consistent deprecation timeline or migration guide. Since 3.0.0 is a major version, these aliases should either be cleanly removed or explicitly annotated with removal timelines.
recommendation: Establish a 3.0.0 cutoff: remove all Wc* aliases in this release since it is a major version, or annotate each with @deprecated since 0.x.0, will be removed in 4.0.0 with a matching breaking change changeset entry.

finding: hx-button maintains a static _VALID_VARIANTS array to runtime-validate the variant property even though the property is already typed as a TypeScript literal union. The runtime guard is a redundant layer that will silently diverge from the type definition over time.
recommendation: Remove _VALID_VARIANTS and the validation block in updated(). The literal union type is the authoritative constraint.

finding: The _parseInput method in hx-number-input contains 'if (raw === null)' where raw is typed as string. In TypeScript strict mode a string cannot be null — this is dead code from a JavaScript-era guard that was not cleaned up during the strict migration.
recommendation: Remove the '|| raw === null' branch. If null inputs are genuinely possible, type the parameter as 'string | null'.

finding: The drupal-starter README states 'Content rendered in Twig is visible in the HTML before JavaScript loads' but this only applies to slotted light DOM content — content rendered inside Shadow DOM is not accessible until JS hydrates. The distinction is not made in the documentation.
recommendation: Clarify progressive enhancement documentation to distinguish between slotted content (pre-JS accessible) and internal component chrome (requires JS).

finding: No root-level README.md exists for the monorepo. CLAUDE.md contains comprehensive agent instructions but there is no developer-facing onboarding document explaining the tech stack, local setup commands, workspace structure, or contribution workflow for human contributors or new team members.
recommendation: Create a root README.md with prerequisites, setup steps, workspace overview, dev server ports, and links to each app's documentation.
